newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. urges Philippines to impose new copyright law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Philippines to impose new copyright law.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to the Philippines, Thomas Hubbard, has urged the Philippines to pass an intellectual property rights bill or else it could be placed on the U.S. priority watchlist.

"If for some reason the legislation is not passed, there will be considerable pressure on the administration to move the Philippines to the priority watchlist," Hubbard said in a letter to Philippines trade secretary Cesar Bautista, a copy of which was released by the trade department on Wednesday.
If placed on the priority watchlist, the Philippines could lose its privilege of the duty-free access that is granted to some of its computer products by the United States.
Bautista has been lobbying for immediate passage of the bill, but congressional deliberations on the measure are yet to start.
